conflicts.point: Whether pre-deployment safety audits or continuous runtime telemetry provide superior protection against cascading systemic errors in multi-agent systems.

positions.stance: Mandatory pre-deployment safety gates are required to evaluate the total blast radius of multi-agent networks because localized metrics miss cumulative compounding errors.
Dynamic runtime telemetry and continuous feedback loops catch operational drift and cascading classification shifts significantly faster than static pre-market reviews.

verdicts.conflict: Whether pre-deployment safety audits or continuous runtime telemetry provide superior protection against cascading systemic errors in multi-agent systems.
verdicts.rationale: Both positions present unverified empirical claims about error detection speeds without citing comparative benchmarks or deployment data from multi-agent enterprise systems. The safetyist claim relies on theoretical compounding risks, while the accelerationist claim assumes runtime telemetry outpaces static reviews without empirical proof of scale.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Comparative empirical trials measuring error containment rates and detection latency between static pre-deployment gates and continuous runtime telemetry in production environments.
